title: Neurobiology (HL) Adventure 1: Neurons and action potentials
welcome_lead: Today you'll fire a spike — HL detail on neurons and the action potential.
meta_desc: Biology HL — neuron structure, action potential, Na/K channels, myelin, saltatory conduction.
final_note: You learned neurons fire all-or-nothing action potentials via Na⁺ and K⁺ voltage-gated channels, refractory period prevents back-propagation, myelin speeds conduction.

walkthroughs.body_html:
At rest, inside of neuron is -70 mV.

Maintained by:
- Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase — 3 Na⁺ out, 2 K⁺ in per ATP.
- K⁺ leak channels — K⁺ slowly diffuses out, creating negativity inside.

Stimulus depolarises to threshold (-55 mV) → opens voltage-gated Na⁺ channels.

Na⁺ rushes in → +30 mV (depolarisation).

Na⁺ channels inactivate; K⁺ channels open → K⁺ exits → repolarisation, slight hyperpolarisation.

The brief refractory period when Na⁺ channels are inactivated ensures the AP travels in one direction.

Schwann cells (PNS) or oligodendrocytes (CNS) wrap axons in myelin (lipid-rich, insulating).

APs jump between nodes of Ranvier — saltatory conduction, up to 120 m/s vs ~1 m/s in unmyelinated.

Multiple sclerosis is autoimmune demyelination — slows or blocks signals.

mcqs.q: When you are too hot, what happens to the arterioles in your skin?
options: The blood vessels move up to the surface of the skin to release heat.
Capillaries split open to release blood and cool the body.
Antibodies are tiny knives that physically cut pathogens apart.
They vasodilate — more blood flows close to the skin surface, releasing heat to the environment by radiation.

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between mitosis and meiosis?
options: Capillaries split open to release blood and cool the body.
Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells; meiosis produces four genetically different haploid cells (gametes).
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Mitosis and meiosis both produce gametes; they are basically the same.

mcqs.q: What makes antibodies effective against pathogens?
options: Capillaries split open to release blood and cool the body.
Antibodies are general-purpose proteins that work against any pathogen.
Antibodies are tiny knives that physically cut pathogens apart.
They have a specific shape complementary to antigens on a particular pathogen, marking it for destruction or neutralising it.
